messages.content: You validate one complete story arc. Return one small JSON object only. Missing source coverage is a blocking error.

Check the proposed arc against the source story.

SOURCE COVERAGE RULE:
Walk through the SOURCE STORY in chronological order before judging the arc.
Every explicit visible action or visible state that establishes a distinct point in the source timeline must be represented by at least one required_event in the arc, in the same order.
Do not dismiss an explicit source action merely because it is calm, introductory, mundane, or not part of the main conflict.
Examples of source actions/states that require coverage when explicitly stated: a character cooking breakfast before danger arrives; a character already driving before a crash; a character sleeping before an intruder enters.
Descriptive attributes such as hair color alone do not require their own event.
Only after all explicit source timeline actions/states are represented may sparse beats be filled with connective jobs.

Reject if any explicit source timeline action/state is missing from required_events.
Return the FIRST missing source action/state as the issue.

SOURCE STORY
--- STORY START ---
A realistic action film about a woman, Amy, protecting her two kids (Will and Amber) from a zombie apocalypse.
Amy is at home on a normal day, wearing a tight, black tank top and denim jeans, cooking breakfast for her young kids.
Suddenly, a zombie breaks the kitchen door window and Amy sees the danger. She rushes her kids to the basement, gets them inside, and then locks the door.
She retrieves her hidden arsenal consisting of a pistol and a katana. She equips the weapons.

The majority of the film is Amy killing (dismembering, decapitating, etc.) zombies as they try and attack her.
Amy kills the last of the zombies, her house now soaked in blood. She lets her kids out of the basement.
--- STORY END ---
